newsitem.title: CHINA: Japan to extend 40 bln yen loan to Shanghai airport.
newsitem.headline: Japan to extend 40 bln yen loan to Shanghai airport.

text.p: Japan is to extend loans worth 40 billion yen to Shanghai's second international airport, scheduled to open in the east of the city in 1999, the China Daily said on Wednesday.

The new airport would cost 13.3 billion yuan ($1.6 billion), of which 3.6 billion yuan would come from the municipal government, three billion yuan from a State Development Bank loan and 40 billion yen ($355.65 million) from the Japanese government, it said.
China has been requesting 16.5 billion yen worth of yen loans for the airport now under construction in the Pudong Development Zone, 30 km (19 miles) from Shanghai's city centre.
The loan is a part of the 580 billion yen in yen loans to China planned for the 1996-1998 fiscal year period by the Japanese government.
